purpose: S5: declared algorithm-assisted whole-body gait warm-up (six legs, 42 joints), no neural claim
why: All earlier work stepped one leg with the other five holding fixed targets. The user's authorised route is algorithm-assisted physical walking first, then neural take-over. This tries a real alternating tripod gait over all six legs.
interface: unchanged incremental actuators; action in [-1,1]^42 mapped to joint target rates within the engineering limit of 2 rad/s; native torque and angle limits remain enforced
controller: declared algorithm-assisted warm-up: body-frame foot trajectories (stance ramp back, swing ramp forward with lift) tracked by resolved-rate control using the thorax-relative Jacobian, plus a body-height feedback term
authorised_by: user instruction: algorithm plus physics simulation should walk a few steps first, then neural take-over; this stage is labelled algorithm-assisted and is not counted as neural autonomous movement

physics: core_v2 (COM-referenced adhesion wrench fix), frozen XML, derived triad world; no qpos/qvel writes after reset, no root translation, no pose locking, no external support force
preregistered_outcomes: if a configuration satisfies all five frozen gates, that is an algorithm-assisted walking result and the take-over stage becomes the next step
if no configuration satisfies all gates, record which gate fails and the best measured values; a failure here is not evidence about the body's limits
no outcome may be described as neural autonomous walking, connectome capability, or frozen-body acceptance
limits: SI calibration NOT_ESTABLISHED. No injury. Teacher and replacement ANN remain separate from connectome capability.
